title: ShellBench Released: Advanced AI Models Such as GPT-6Astra Fail Over One-Third of Everyday Tasks

content_html:
The OpenClaw Foundation, together with several other organizations, has released ShellBench, a benchmark for AI agents. The research shows that even advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta still have a high failure rate when handling everyday personal tasks, raising challenges for reliability and safety.

ShellBench was developed through a collaboration between the OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and researchers at the University of California, Berkeley. It is based on more than 10 million anonymized real-world AI agent interactions and evaluates models' ability to carry out multi-step tasks in complex personal data environments such as email, calendars, spreadsheets, receipts, and chat histories. The tests found that all models had a task failure rate above one-third, and 15.7% of attempts violated at least one safety requirement.

In terms of consistency, even OpenAI GPT-6Astra, the highest-scoring model, had less than a 50% chance of succeeding on all three repeated runs of a task under the same conditions. In specific scenarios, the agent failed to correctly record a child's school pickup schedule in 79.5% of cases, failed to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts, and recommended duplicate or incorrect bill payments in 40.3% of cases.

The research also found that the model itself generally has a greater impact on task performance than the agent framework, but the stronger the model, the more pronounced the performance differences caused by the choice of framework. For example, GPT-6Astra outperformed Claude Fable5.2 in the Pi framework, but fell behind when tested in Claude Code. Meta's Muse Wonder Full scored 56% in the Pi framework and dropped to 38.1% in Claude Code.

It is worth noting that these tests did not use the native runtime frameworks of Muse, OpenAI Dots, or Claude Duet, so the results do not fully represent what consumers experience in actual use. As personal AI assistants become more widely adopted, ShellBench also highlights a key issue currently facing the industry: agents must not only complete tasks, but also have reliable information judgment, privacy protection, and safe execution capabilities.
